title: Radio outburst from a massive (proto)star. II. A portrait in space and time of the expanding radio jet from S255IR NIRS 3
question: What is the spatial and temporal evolution of the expanding radio jet from the massive (proto)star S255IR NIRS 3 following its accretion outburst?

recipe.goal: Measure multi-epoch radio and millimetre continuum flux densities
recipe.method: Integrate flux density inside a polygonal shape encompassing the compact source across VLA bands and ALMA 3 mm maps; subtract fiducial large-scale lobe flux (1.8 mJy at 6 GHz, 1.0 mJy at 10 GHz) in D-array when needed; separate NE and SW components at 3 mm.
assumptions: Large-scale lobes have constant flux in time; check source at 06h12m53.61s +18d00m26.4s is non-variable

recipe.goal: Track spatial expansion of the radio jet peak
recipe.method: Fit a 2D Gaussian to sub-arcsecond VLA K-band (1.3 cm) maps to determine peak positions over time, and combine with the ALMA 3 mm NE peak positions and the OLHKP peak position to compute projected expansion velocities.
key_parameters: Position uncertainty represented as 1/5 of the synthesised beam
assumptions: Protostar is located at the stationary SW peak of the 3 mm continuum emission (06h 12m 54.012s, +17d 59m 23.04s); distance d = 1.78 kpc

recipe.goal: Compute 3 mm spectral index maps and decompose dust vs. free-free emission
recipe.method: Create continuum maps for the four ALMA Band 3 spectral windows (85.2, 87.2, 97.2, 99.2 GHz) with identical clean beams, fit pixel-by-pixel spectral index alpha where all four fluxes exceed 5 sigma, and calculate the free-free flux fraction R_S/(1+R_S).
key_parameters: 5 sigma threshold across all 4 bands; nu_1 = 85.2 GHz, nu_2 = 99.2 GHz
assumptions: Optically thin dust emission with S_nu^d propto nu^gamma (gamma = 2 to 4, dust opacity index beta = 0 to 2) and optically thin free-free emission with S_nu^ff propto nu^-0.1

recipe.goal: Fit 2D spatial morphology of the NE lobe in ALMA 3 mm maps and derive jet expansion law
recipe.method: Generate synthetic 2D brightness temperature maps of an optically thin jet (T_B = T_0 (y/y_0)^-3), convolve with the ALMA beam, fit to the observed NE lobe at t = 1061 and 1881 days to find y_0, y_m, and theta_0, and solve the momentum-conserving deceleration equation for T and y_m0.
key_parameters: t = 1061 days and t = 1881 days; v_0 = 900 km s^-1; psi = 10 deg
assumptions: 3 mm emission in the NE lobe is optically thin everywhere (T_B = T_0 (y/y_0)^-3); jet expands conserving momentum into an ambient medium with density propto r^-2

recipe.goal: Fit multi-epoch radio continuum spectra and derive jet physical evolution
recipe.method: Fit the modified mono-polar Reynolds jet model (Eq. A.10) to each VLA continuum spectrum at nu >= 6 GHz across 16 epochs by varying theta_0, r_0, and Lambda, then compute the ionised jet mass M_i(t) and ejection-to-accretion ratio R_e.
key_parameters: Fixed T_0 = 10^4 K, psi = 10 deg, y_m(t) from Eq. 6, mu = 1.67e-24 g; grid ranges theta_0 = 3-50 deg, r_0 = 50-300 au, Lambda = 10^-10 to 10^-7 M_sun yr^-1 / (km s^-1)
assumptions: Mono-polar thermal jet during VLA monitoring; standard spherical scaling (n propto r^-2, T_0, v_0, x_0, theta_0 independent of r); pyramidal geometry valid for theta_0 < 90 deg; emission at nu < 6 GHz excluded due to non-thermal contamination

score_reason: The paper provides complete flux density tables, explicit analytical derivations of both the expansion law and the modified Reynolds thermal jet equations in the appendices, and full best-fit parameter tables; only minor imaging parameters (cell size, cleaning thresholds, polygon vertices) and custom fitting scripts are unstated.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA (2018.1.00864.S) and VLA (16A-424, 16B-427, 17B-045) datasets, fully tabulated flux densities and model parameters, and closed-form analytical equations in the appendices make both the continuum/spectral-index imaging and the time-dependent jet model fits highly suitable for automated reproduction.
